title: The Dhvanyaloka of Anandavardhana with the Locana of Abhinavagupta

publication.publisher_or_container: Harvard University Press (Harvard Oriental Series Vol. 49)

verification.verification_notes: Silo mirror of the verified shared record src-anandavardhana-dhvanyaloka-1990. Used here for the broader claim that aesthetic effect (including the effect of a tense or forceful passage) is judged by propriety and suggested meaning rather than by surface intensity. The specific Sanskrit concept aucitya (propriety of fit, including fit of moment) is a specialist lead not page-verified here; see dossier evidence-incomplete note.

translation.translator: Daniel H. H. Ingalls, J. M. Masson, M. V. Patwardhan
limitations: Sanskrit aesthetic technical terminology requires bilingual cross-referencing.
aucitya (propriety) is most developed in Kshemendra's later poetics, outside this edition; that extension is flagged as evidence-incomplete.
